subject: general
question: The third order central moment of normal distribution is:
solution:
The correct answer is** 0.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **The third order central moment of normal distribution is 0:**

 
 
• In statistics, the third order central moment is a measure of the asymmetry (skewness) of a probability distribution.
 
• For a normal distribution, which is symmetric about its mean, the skewness is zero. Hence, the third order central moment is zero.
 
• This property is crucial in financial enterprises when modeling asset returns. A normal distribution assumption implies no skewness, leading to simpler risk management and forecasting models.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The third order central moment is positive:**

 
 
• This is incorrect. A positive third order central moment indicates a positively skewed distribution, which is not the case for a normal distribution.
 
 
 
• **The third order central moment is 1:**
 
 
• This is incorrect. The value of 1 does not represent the third order central moment of a normal distribution. The skewness measure for a normal distribution is zero.
 
 
 
• **The third order central moment is negative:**
 
 
• This is incorrect. A negative third order central moment indicates a negatively skewed distribution, which is not applicable for a normal distribution.
